issues.detail: This diff does three things: (1) extract sign/verify into a shared util, (2) replace per-wallet sign_message with current_p2_puzzle_hash helpers, (3) add tests for sign_message_by_id and sign_message_by_address. Each is reviewable on its own and bisectable on its own. Submitted together they make the diff harder to read and harder to revert if one piece regresses. THREE-PATCHES.

issues.description: Duplicated signing-mode branch logic in sign_message and verify_signature
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py:sign_message and verify_signature each carry their own if/elif chain over SigningMode, and the property signing_mode_enum on the request types is a third copy of similar branching. The whole point of extracting a library is to have one place where the mode-to-bytes mapping lives. Pull the mode-to-message-bytes computation into one helper and call it from both sign and verify. Right now we have parallel ladders that will drift.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is a leftover lie
issues.detail: The new free function carries ':param request:' in its docstring even though it takes no request object - it takes five keyword arguments. This was copy-pasted from the RPC method and never updated. Maintainer-six-years-from-now reads that and wonders where 'request' is. Fix the docstring or delete it.

issues.description: Module-level signing_mode_enum function shadows the property of the same name
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines a top-level function signing_mode_enum(request) and then defines a @property signing_mode_enum on two classes that calls it. Same name, two scopes, easy to misread which one is called. Either rename the helper (_compute_signing_mode) or make it a static/class method. Naming collisions like this are gratuitous.

A new module-private @dataclass(kw_only=True, frozen=True) with two fields (pubkey, signature) is introduced just to be unpacked at every call site into a separate response type (SignMessageByAddressResponse / SignMessageByIDResponse). The previous code returned a tuple[G1Element, G2Element] and that was fine for an internal helper. Adding a class that nothing else uses, just to wrap a 2-tuple, is the kind of abstraction-for-its-own-sake that adds nothing. Return the tuple, or have callers consume the existing response types directly. BAD-TASTE.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum property is called repeatedly per request - compute once
issues.detail: In sign_message_by_address and sign_message_by_id the property request.signing_mode_enum is invoked three times in the same function (once for mode, once for the response value). The property re-runs the if/elif ladder each access. Bind it to a local variable once. Cheap fix, removes wasted work and makes the call sites read better.

issues.description: Error message inconsistency between DID wallet ValueErrors
issues.detail: did_wallet.current_p2_puzzle_hash raises 'Missing DID inner puzzle.' for one path and 'Invalid DID inner puzzle.' for the other; the original code said 'Invalid inner DID puzzle.' Word-order shuffled for no reason. Either revert the wording or leave it - just don't churn an error message in a refactor PR.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address never asserts the verification result
issues.detail: The new test calls client.verify_signature(...) and discards the return value. The endpoint returns VerifySignatureResponse(isValid=bool, error=...) which can come back isValid=False with no exception. A test that doesn't assert the thing it's testing is decoration. Add `assert res.isValid is True`.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic placed on base Wallet but called via main_wallet only
issues.detail: The new helper sits on Wallet, but every caller in wallet_rpc_api uses `self.service.wallet_state_manager.main_wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(...)`. It does not depend on any wallet instance state - it's pure. Either make it a module-level function in signing.py (where it belongs) or a @staticmethod. Hanging it off main_wallet as an instance method on the base class is misleading; it implies per-wallet behavior that does not exist.

issues.description: Tests duplicate the implementation's mode-to-bytes ladder
issues.detail: test_sign_message_by_nft_id manually constructs `Program.to((CHIP_0002_SIGN_MESSAGE_PREFIX, message)).get_tree_hash()` and `bytes(message, 'utf-8')` etc. inline to verify each mode. That is the same ladder as in signing.py. The natural test is to call verify_signature() with the appropriate mode - which is the function the PR just shipped. Otherwise the test is a parallel reimplementation that will pass even if both sides drift together.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The direction is right - pulling sign/verify out of the RPC into a library is the correct shape, and the per-wallet sign_message methods becoming current_p2_puzzle_hash is a clean simplification. But the patch leaves duplicated mode-to-bytes ladders in three places (sign, verify, request-property), introduces a one-shot SignMessageResponse dataclass that earns nothing, ships a verify_signature docstring that still talks about a 'request' parameter that does not exist, and bundles three distinct changes into one diff. The new test_sign_message_by_address forgets to assert isValid. Fix the dedup, the docstring, the assertion, and consider splitting; then it lands.
